Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 96, verses 1–4:

Meccan, and it has two hundred and eighty letters, seventy-two words, and nineteen verses.

Al-Jabbari told us: Ibn Hayyan told us: al-Farqadi told us: Isma'il ibn Amr told us: Yusuf ibn Atiyya told us: Harun ibn Kathir told us: Zayd ibn Aslam told us, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Iqra' bi-ismi Rabbika, it is as if he had recited the whole Mufassal" [184] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/396.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created,﴾ ﴿created man from a clot.﴾ That is, blood; its singular is ʿalaqah. The plural is used although the word "insan" (man) is singular, because it carries the sense of a plural. This is the first surah to be revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the Qur'an, and the first of it to be revealed was five verses from its beginning up to His saying ﴿what he did not know﴾. This is the view of most scholars.

Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hamdun and Abd Allah ibn Hamid told us: Ibn al-Sharqi told us:

Muhammad ibn Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: Urwa informed me, from Aisha, that she said: The first thing with which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began receiving revelation was true dreams in sleep. He would not see a dream except that it came like the break of dawn. Then Allah made seclusion dear to him, so he would go to Hira' and devote himself to worship there, which is tahannuth, during nights of a set number, and he would take provisions for that. Then he would return to Khadija, and she would provide him with the like, until the Truth came upon him while he was in the cave of Hira'.

[Aisha] said: The angel came to him and said: "Read." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I said to him: 'I am not a reader.' He seized me and pressed me until I reached the limit of exertion, then he released me and said: 'Read.' I said: 'I am not a reader.' He seized me and pressed me a second time until I reached the limit of exertion, then he released me and said: 'Read.' I said: 'I am not a reader.' He seized me and pressed me a third time until I reached the limit of exertion, then he released me and said: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾, until ﴿what he did not know﴾."

So he returned with it, his shoulders trembling, until he entered upon Khadija and said: "Wrap me up, wrap me up." They wrapped him until the fear had left him. Then he said: "O Khadija, what is wrong with me?" [185] and he told her the news, and said: "I fear for myself." She said to him:

"No indeed, rejoice! By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. Verily you join the ties of kinship, you speak the truth, you bear the burdens of others, you provide for the destitute, you honour the guest, and you help in the calamities of the truth."

Then Khadija set off with him and brought him to Waraqa ibn Nawfal ibn Asad ibn Abd al-ʿUzza ibn Qusayy, who was the cousin of Khadija. He had become a Christian in the pre-Islamic period, and he used to write the Arabic script, and he was an elderly man who had gone blind. Khadija said: "O cousin, listen to your nephew." Waraqa ibn Nawfal said: "O nephew, what do you see?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed him of what he had seen. Waraqa said: "This is the Namus (the confidant of revelation) that was sent down to Musa. Would that I were young in it! Would that I were alive when your people expel you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Will they expel me?" [186] Waraqa said: "Yes. No man has ever come with the like of what you have brought except that he was opposed and harmed. If your day finds me, I will support you with a mighty support." Then Waraqa did not long survive, and revelation paused for a period, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved, as we have been told, a grief that made him many times prepare to throw himself from the summits of high mountains. Whenever he reached the peak of a mountain to cast himself down from it, Jibril (peace be upon him) appeared to him and said: "O Muhammad, you are truly the Messenger of Allah." His restlessness would be calmed and his soul would be reassured, and he would return. When the pause in revelation lengthened upon him, he would again go out, and whenever he reached the peak of a mountain, Jibril would appear to him and say to him the like of that [187] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 8/68, ed. Dar al-Fikr. It is astonishing that this is attributed to the Messenger, the Prophet of mercy! How is it conceivable that tranquillity reached Waraqa but did not reach one who is more excellent than Waraqa by degrees? How is it conceivable that the Prophet sent to complete good character and to forbid what is prohibited would think of and intend suicide and self-killing? And more astonishing is that they attributed this to him, may the prayers of those who pray be upon him, several times, and then he returns to what Jibril forbade him! It is as if they wish to portray him like a child or a simpleton! Is our Prophet not the best of the people of his time? Then what is the matter with Waraqa, who was wiser, more guided, more perceptive and more intelligent than him? May Allah protect us from error.]].

Al-Zuhri said: Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) speak about the pause in revelation, and in his account he said: "While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky, so I raised my head, and behold, the angel who came to me at Hira' was sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I was seized with terror from him, so I returned and said: 'Wrap me up, wrap me up, cover me.'" [188] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/4; Tafsir al-Tabari: 29/179.]] Then Allah the Exalted sent down: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾ up to His saying ﴿and abandon the uncleanness﴾. Before the prayer was made obligatory, the "uncleanness" means idols. Then what was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of the Qur'an after "Iqra'" and "al-Muddaththir" was: ﴿Nun. By the pen﴾ up to His saying ﴿And indeed you are of a tremendous character﴾, and then ﴿By the morning brightness﴾.

Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Ibn Jarir, who said: Ibn Abi al-Shawarib told us:

Abd al-Wahid told us: Sulayman al-Shaybani told us: Abd Allah ibn Shaddad told us: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) received ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾, then Jibril delayed coming to him, so Khadija said to him: "I think only that your Lord has forsaken you." So Allah sent down: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it becomes still. Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you.﴾

Abd Allah ibn Hamid told us: Makki told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Bashir told us: Sufyan told us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from Urwa, from Aisha, who said: The first surah revealed was ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾.

Abd Allah ibn Hamid told us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us: Ali ibn Harb told us:

Abu Amir al-Aqadi told us, from Qurra ibn Khalid, from Abu Raja' al-Utaridi, who said: Abu Musa used to recite the Qur'an to us in this mosque, and we would sit before him in circles. As if I were looking at him now, in two white garments, from him I took this surah: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾ [[Surat al-ʿAlaq: 1.]].

And he said: The first surah revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the Opening of the Book (al-Fatiha).

Muhammad ibn Hamdawayh and Abd Allah ibn Hamid told us, both saying: Muhammad told us: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar told us: Yunus ibn Bukayr told us, from Yunus ibn Amr, from his father, from Abu Maysara Amr ibn Shurahbil, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Khadija: "When I am alone by myself, I hear a call, and by Allah, I have feared that this may be a matter [of concern]."

She said: "Allah forbid! Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would never do that to you. By Allah, you fulfil trusts, you join the ties of kinship, and you speak the truth."

When Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, entered while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was [in the house], Khadija then mentioned it to him and said: "O Atiq, go with Muhammad to Waraqa ibn Nawfal." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered, Abu Bakr took him by the hand and said:

"Come with us to Waraqa." He said: "Who informed you?" He said: "Khadija." So they went to him, and he related to him [the matter]. [Waraqa] said: "When I am alone by myself, I hear a call behind me: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad,' so I set off fleeing into the earth."

He said to him: "Do not do that. When it comes to you, stand firm until you hear what it says, then come to me and inform me." When he was alone, [the voice] called to him: "O Muhammad, say: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [[Surat al-Fatiha: 1–2.]] until ﴿nor of those who are astray﴾ [[Surat al-Fatiha: 7.]]. Say: There is no god but Allah." He came to Waraqa and mentioned that to him. Waraqa said to him: "Rejoice, then rejoice! I bear witness that you are the one whose coming was foretold by the son of Mary, that you are upon the like of the Namus of Musa, that you are a sent Prophet, and that you will be commanded to fight after this day of yours. If that day reaches me, I will certainly fight alongside you." When Waraqa died, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw the priest in Paradise, wearing garments of silk, because he believed in me and affirmed me" [189] [[In full in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 1/116.]], meaning Waraqa. They said: Waraqa also said:

If it is true, O Khadija, then know
that your report to us: Ahmad is one sent.
Jibril comes to him, and Mika'il with them,
from Allah, revelation that expands the breast, descending.

Whoever is victorious thereby is honoured for his religion,
and the misguided, the wretched, the astray, is ruined by it.
A band of them is in its gardens,
and another is hauled about in the chains of Hell. [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/398.]]

﴿Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous,﴾ al-Kalbi said: that is, the Forbearing toward the ignorance of worship, and does not hasten to punish them. ﴿Who taught by the pen﴾, that is, writing and the script.

Ibn Fanjawayh told us: Ibn Shayba told us: Ibn Mahan told us: Muhammad ibn Ayyub ibn Hisham al-Muzani told us: Abu al-Hasan Asim ibn Ali ibn Asim and Abd Allah ibn Asim al-Jamani told us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Rashid told us, from Muslim ibn Musa, who said: Amr ibn Shu'ayb informed me, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: I said: "O Prophet of Allah, shall I write down what I hear from you of hadith?" He said: "Yes, write, for Allah ﴿taught by the pen﴾" [190] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/120.]].
